card.summary_ko: 1876년 운요호 사건 뒤 조선과 일본이 강화도에서 맺은 12款의 수호조규로, 조선이 근대적 조약 체제에 처음 들어선 계기가 된 불평등 조약이다.
card.summary_en: A 12-article treaty of amity concluded on Ganghwa Island in 1876, after the Unyo incident; the first modern treaty Joseon signed and an unequal one that opened its ports to Japan.
card.edition_ko: 江華島條約 — 중국어 위키문헌, 판 2528032; 원문은 공문서(저작권법 제7조)로 보호 대상이 아니며, 전사는 위키문헌 기여자(CC BY-SA 4.0)

notes.ko:
**저자 (체결 주체)** 이 글은 한 사람의 저작이 아니라 두 정부가 교섭해 서명한 조약문이다. 조선 측 전권은 판중추부사 신헌(1810–1884)과 부관 윤자승이었다. 신헌은 무관 출신 원로로 신미양요(1871) 때 강화 방비를 맡았고, 박규수 등 개국론자와 뜻이 통했다고 평가된다. 당시 조선 조정은 고종의 친정 아래 민씨 척족의 영향력이 커지던 때였고, 개항을 받아들이자는 쪽과 위정척사의 입장에서 반대하는 쪽(최익현 등)으로 갈려 있었다. 일본 측 전권은 육군 중장 겸 개척사 장관 구로다 기요타카(사쓰마 출신, 뒤에 총리)와 부전권 이노우에 가오루(조슈 출신, 뒤에 외무경, 1894년 주조선공사)였다. 메이지 정부는 문명개화와 대외 팽창을 함께 추진하던 정부였다.

**시대적 맥락** 1875년 9월 일본 군함 운요호가 강화도 앞바다에서 조선 포대와 포격을 주고받는 사건(운요호 사건)이 일어났다. 일본은 이를 구실로 이듬해 초 군함을 앞세워 구로다와 이노우에를 보내 수교를 요구했다. 조정에서는 최익현이 도끼를 지니고 궐 앞에 엎드려 개항 반대 상소(지부상소)를 올렸다가 흑산도로 유배되었으나, 결국 교섭이 진행되어 강화부 연무당에서 조약이 조인되었다.

**배경** 조선 병자년 2월 2일, 일본 메이지 9년 2월 26일(양력 1876년 2월 26일)에 조인되었다. 이 앱의 목록에는 2월 27일로 적혀 있는데, 한국 쪽 문헌에는 음력 2월 3일에 해당하는 27일로 적은 것도 있다. 본문에 적힌 날짜(병자 2월 초2일, 메이지 9년 2월 26일)는 26일이다. 정식 이름은 조일수호조규(병자수호조규)이며, 같은 해 8월 부록과 무역규칙이 따로 체결되어 세부 사항(무관세 무역 등)을 정했다. 이 판본은 중국어 위키문헌 「江華島條約」의 전사본이다.

**의의** 조선이 근대 조약 체제에 처음 편입된 조약이다. 제1조 "朝鮮國自主之邦"을 두고, 일본은 청과의 종속 관계를 부정하려는 뜻이 있었다고 보는 견해가 많고, 조선과 청 쪽에서는 '자주'를 속방 관계와 양립하는 말로 이해할 여지도 있어 해석이 갈린다. 불평등한 성격은 치외법권(제10조), 일본인의 해안 측량권(제7조), 관세 규정의 부재(제9조) 등에서 드러난다. 부산에 더해 원산(1880), 인천(1883)이 차례로 열렸다.

**형식과 주제** 한문 공문서 형식의 12款 조약이다. 앞머리에 전권 위임 사실을, 끝에 날짜와 서명·인을 둔다. 주제는 외교 사절 교환(제2조), 공문 언어(제3조: 일본은 자국 글에 한문 번역을 10년간 붙이고 조선은 한문 사용), 개항장과 무역(제4·5·9조), 표류·난파 구호(제6조), 영사 재판(제10조)이다.

**읽기 도움**
- 嗣後(사후): 앞으로, 이후
- 準聽(준청): 허락하다
- 款(관): 조항
- 全權辦理大臣(전권판리대신): 전권대신
- 歲遣船(세견선): 매년 보내던 무역선
- 鈐印(검인): 도장을 찍다
- 左/右(좌/우): 세로쓰기에서 '아래/위'
- 眞文(진문): 한문(漢文)
- 開國四百八十五年: 1392년을 원년으로 센 조선 연호
notes.en:
**About the author (signatories)** This is not an individual's writing but a treaty negotiated and signed by two governments. For Joseon the plenipotentiary was Shin Heon (1810-1884), Chief of the Privy Council Office, with Yun Ja-seung as deputy. Shin was a veteran military official who had been in charge of the Ganghwa defences during the American expedition of 1871, and is generally regarded as sympathetic to officials such as Bak Gyu-su who favoured opening the country. The Joseon court was under King Gojong's personal rule, with the Min in-law faction gaining influence, and was split between those willing to open the ports and conservative Neo-Confucian "defend orthodoxy, reject heterodoxy" (wijeong cheoksa) opponents such as Choe Ik-hyeon. For Japan the plenipotentiary was Lieutenant-General Kuroda Kiyotaka (from Satsuma; head of the Hokkaido Colonisation Office; later prime minister), with Inoue Kaoru (from Choshu; later foreign minister and, in 1894, minister to Korea) as deputy. The Meiji government pursued "civilisation and enlightenment" and overseas expansion together.

**Historical context** In September 1875 the Japanese gunboat Unyo exchanged fire with Joseon forts off Ganghwa Island (the Unyo incident). Japan used it as a pretext to send Kuroda and Inoue with warships in early 1876 to demand a treaty. At court, Choe Ik-hyeon laid an axe before the palace gate in a memorial against opening the ports and was exiled to Heuksan Island, but negotiations went ahead and the treaty was signed at the Yeonmudang drill hall in Ganghwa.

**Background** It was signed on the 2nd day of the 2nd month of the byeongja year (Meiji 9, 26 February 1876). The app's catalogue lists 27 February, and some Korean references also give the 27th (the 3rd lunar day); the dates written in the text itself (byeongja 2nd month 2nd day; Meiji 9, 2nd month 26th) correspond to the 26th. Its formal name is the Joseon-Japan Treaty of Amity (Byeongja suho jogyu); a supplement and trade regulations followed in August of the same year to settle details (including duty-free trade). This edition is the Chinese Wikisource transcription of "江華島條約".

**Significance** It first brought Joseon into the modern treaty system. Article 1, "Joseon is a self-governing state", is read by many historians as Japan's attempt to deny Qing suzerainty, while on the Joseon and Qing side "jaju" could be understood as compatible with a tributary relationship, so interpretations differ. The treaty's unequal character shows in extraterritoriality (Art. 10), Japanese survey rights over the coast (Art. 7) and the absence of any customs provision (Art. 9). Wonsan (1880) and Incheon (1883) were opened in addition to Busan.

**Form and themes** A twelve-article treaty in official Chinese, opening with the plenipotentiaries' credentials and closing with dates, names and seals. Themes: exchange of envoys (Art. 2), language of correspondence (Art. 3: Japan uses its own script with a Chinese translation for ten years; Joseon uses Chinese), ports and trade (Arts. 4, 5, 9), relief of the shipwrecked (Art. 6), consular jurisdiction (Art. 10).

**Reading help**
- 嗣後 (sahu): henceforth
- 準聽 (junceong): to permit
- 款 (gwan): article, clause
- 全權辦理大臣: plenipotentiary
- 歲遣船 (segyeonseon): the annual trade ships Joseon allowed Japan
- 鈐印 (geomin): to affix a seal
- 左 / 右: "below / above" in vertical writing
- 眞文 (jinmun): "true script", i.e. Chinese
- 開國四百八十五年: Joseon's era count from 1392

paragraphs.orig: 大日本國與大朝鮮國素敦友誼，歷有年所，今因視兩國情意未洽，欲重修舊好，以固親睦，是以日本國政府簡特命全權辦理大臣陸軍中將兼參議開拓長官黑田清隆、副全權辦理大臣議官井上馨詣朝鮮國江華府，朝鮮國政府簡判中樞府事申櫶、副總管尹滋承，各遵所奉諭旨，議立條款，開列於左：
paragraphs.reading: 대일본국여대조선국소돈우의, 역유년소, 금인시양국정의미흡, 욕중수구호, 이고친목, 시이일본국정부간특명전권판리대신육군중장겸참의개척장관흑전청륭, 부전권판리대신의관정상형예조선국강화부, 조선국정부간판중추부사신헌, 부총관윤자승, 각준소봉유지, 의립조관, 개열어좌:
paragraphs.en: The Empire of Great Japan and the Kingdom of Great Joseon have long maintained friendly relations, over many years. Now, seeing that the sentiments of the two countries are not in accord, and desiring to restore the old amity and so strengthen their friendship, the government of Japan has appointed as Envoy Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary Kuroda Kiyotaka, Lieutenant-General of the Army, Councillor and Chief of the Colonisation Office, and as Deputy Plenipotentiary Inoue Kaoru, Councillor of the Senate, who have come to Ganghwa Prefecture in Joseon; and the government of Joseon has appointed Shin Heon, Chief of the Privy Council Office, and Yun Ja-seung, Vice-Director-General. Each, in accordance with the instructions he has received, has deliberated and drawn up articles, set out below:

paragraphs.orig: 第一款　朝鮮國自主之邦，保有與日本國平等之權。嗣後兩國欲表和親之實，須以彼此同等之禮相待，不可毫有侵越猜嫌。宜先將從前為交情阻塞之患諸例規一切革除，務開擴寬裕弘通之法，以期永遠相安。
paragraphs.reading: 제일관 조선국자주지방, 보유여일본국평등지권. 사후양국욕표화친지실, 수이피차동등지례상대, 불가호유침월시혐. 의선장종전위교정조색지환제례규일절혁제, 무개확관유홍통지법, 이기영원상안.
paragraphs.en: Article 1. Joseon, being a self-governing state, holds rights equal to those of Japan. From now on, if the two countries wish to show the reality of peace and amity, they must treat one another with equal courtesy and must not in the least encroach upon or suspect one another. They shall first abolish all the rules and precedents that have hitherto obstructed friendship, and strive to open up generous and broad-minded ways, so as to live in peace with each other forever.

paragraphs.orig: 第二款　日本國政府自今十五個月後隨時派使臣到朝鮮國京城，得親接禮曹判書，商議交際事務。該使臣駐留久暫，共任時宜。朝鮮國政府亦隨時派使臣到日本國東京，得親接外務卿，商議交際事務。該使臣駐留久暫，亦任時宜。
paragraphs.reading: 제이관 일본국정부자금십오개월후수시파사신도조선국경성, 득친접예조판서, 상의교제사무. 해사신주류구잠, 공임시의. 조선국정부역수시파사신도일본국동경, 득친접외무경, 상의교제사무. 해사신주류구잠, 역임시의.
paragraphs.en: Article 2. Fifteen months from now, the Japanese government may at any time send an envoy to the capital of Joseon, where he shall be received in person by the Minister of Rites to discuss matters of intercourse. The length of the envoy's stay shall be as suits the occasion. The Joseon government may likewise at any time send an envoy to Tokyo in Japan, where he shall be received in person by the Minister of Foreign Affairs to discuss matters of intercourse. The length of that envoy's stay shall likewise be as suits the occasion.

paragraphs.orig: 第三款　嗣後兩國往來公文，日本用其國文，自今十年間別具譯漢文一本。朝鮮用真文。
paragraphs.en: Article 3. From now on, in official correspondence between the two countries, Japan shall use its own script and, for ten years from now, shall attach a separate Chinese translation. Joseon shall use true script (Chinese).

paragraphs.orig: 第四款　朝鮮國釜山草梁項立有日本公館，久已為兩國人民通商之區。今應革除從前慣例及歲遣船等事，憑準新立條款，措辦貿易事務。且朝鮮國政府須別開第五款所載之二口，準聽日本國人民往來通商，就該地賃借地基，造營家屋，或僑寓所在人民屋宅，各隨其便。
paragraphs.reading: 제사관 조선국부산초량항립유일본공관, 구이위양국인민통상지구. 금응혁제종전관례급세견선등사, 빙준신립조관, 조판무역사무. 차조선국정부수별개제오관소재지이구, 준청일본국인민왕래통상, 취해지임차지기, 조영가옥, 혹교우소재인민옥택, 각수기편.
paragraphs.en: Article 4. A Japanese mission house has been established at Choryang in Busan, Joseon, and has long been a place of trade between the peoples of the two countries. The former customs, such as the annual dispatch of ships, shall now be abolished, and trade shall be conducted in accordance with the newly established articles. Moreover, the Joseon government shall separately open the two ports referred to in Article 5, and shall permit Japanese subjects to come and go and trade there, to rent land there, build houses, or lodge in the houses of the local people, each as is convenient to them.

paragraphs.orig: 第五款　京圻、忠清、全羅、慶尚、咸鏡五道中，沿海擇便通商之港口二處，指定地名，開口之期日本歷自明治九年二月、朝鮮歷自丙子年二月起算，共為二十個月。
paragraphs.reading: 제오관 경기, 충청, 전라, 경상, 함경오도중, 연해택편통상지항구이처, 지정지명, 개구지기일본력자명치구년이월, 조선력자병자년이월기산, 공위이십개월.
paragraphs.en: Article 5. Among the five provinces of Gyeonggi, Chungcheong, Jeolla, Gyeongsang and Hamgyeong, two coastal ports convenient for trade shall be selected and their names designated. The date of opening shall be counted from the second month of Meiji 9 by the Japanese calendar and from the second month of the byeongja year by the Joseon calendar, making twenty months in all.

paragraphs.orig: 第六款　嗣後日本國船隻在朝鮮國沿海或遭大風，或薪糧窮竭不能達指定港口，即得入隨處沿岸支港避險補缺、修繕船具、買求柴炭等，其在地方供給費用，必由船主賠償。凡是等事地方官民須特別加意憐恤，救援無不至，補給勿敢吝惜。倘兩國船隻在洋破壞，舟人漂至，隨處地方人民即時救卹保全，禀地方官，該官護還其本國，或交付其就近駐留本國官員。
paragraphs.reading: 제육관 사후일본국선척재조선국연해혹조대풍, 혹신량궁갈불능달지정항구, 즉득입수처연안지항피험보결, 수선선구, 매구시탄등, 기재지방공급비용, 필유선주배상. 범시등사지방관민수특별가의련휼, 구원무부지, 보급물감린석. 당양국선척재양파괴, 주인표지, 수처지방인민즉시구휼보전, 품지방관, 해관호환기본국, 혹교부기취근주류본국관원.
paragraphs.en: Article 6. From now on, should Japanese ships on the coast of Joseon meet with great winds, or exhaust their fuel and provisions and be unable to reach a designated port, they may enter any inlet along the coast, wherever it may be, to shelter from danger and make good their shortages, repair their gear and buy firewood and charcoal; the costs of local supply shall be compensated by the shipmaster. In all such matters the local officials and people shall take special care to show compassion, giving aid without fail and supplying without stint. If ships of either country are wrecked at sea and their crews drift ashore, the local people, wherever it may be, shall at once relieve and protect them and report to the local officials, who shall escort them back to their own country or hand them over to officials of their country stationed nearby.

paragraphs.orig: 第七款　朝鮮國沿海島嶼岩礁，從前無經審檢，極為危險。準聽日本國航海者隨時測量海岸，審其位置深淺，編制圖誌，俾兩國船客以得避危就安。
paragraphs.reading: 제칠관 조선국연해도서암초, 종전무경심검, 극위위험. 준청일본국항해자수시측량해안, 심기위치심천, 편제도지, 비양국선객이득피위취안.
paragraphs.en: Article 7. The islands and reefs along the coast of Joseon have never been surveyed and are extremely dangerous. Japanese navigators are permitted to survey the coast at any time, examine the positions and depths, and compile charts and records, so that seafarers of both countries may avoid danger and make for safety.

paragraphs.orig: 第八款　嗣後日本國政府於朝鮮國指定各口，隨時設置管理日本國商民之官，遇有兩國交涉案件，會商所在地方長官辦理。
paragraphs.en: Article 8. From now on, the Japanese government may at any time establish at the ports designated in Joseon an official to manage Japanese merchants and people; whenever cases arise involving both countries, he shall confer with the chief local official and handle them.

paragraphs.orig: 第九款　兩國既經通好，彼此人民各自任意貿易，兩國官吏毫無干預，又不得限制禁阻。倘有兩國商民欺罔炫賣、貸借不償等事，兩國官吏嚴拿該逋商民，令追辦債欠，但兩國政府不能代償。
paragraphs.reading: 제구관 양국기경통호, 피차인민각자임의무역, 양국관리호무간예, 우부득한제금조. 당유양국상민기망현매, 대차불상등사, 양국관리엄나해포상민, 영추판채흠, 단양국정부불능대상.
paragraphs.en: Article 9. Now that the two countries have established friendly relations, their peoples shall each trade as they please, without any interference at all from the officials of either country, and without limitation or prohibition. If merchants of either country defraud, sell by deceit, or borrow without repaying, the officials of both countries shall strictly arrest the absconding merchants and make them pay the debt; but the governments of the two countries cannot pay on their behalf.

paragraphs.orig: 第十款　日本國人民在朝鮮國指定各口，如其犯罪交涉朝鮮國人民，皆歸日本官審斷。如朝鮮國人民犯罪交涉日本國人民，均歸朝鮮官査辦。各據其國律訊斷，毫無回護袒庇，務昭公平允當。
paragraphs.reading: 제십관 일본국인민재조선국지정각구, 여기범죄교섭조선국인민, 개귀일본관심단. 여조선국인민범죄교섭일본국인민, 균귀조선관사판. 각거기국률신단, 호무회호단비, 무소공평윤당.
paragraphs.en: Article 10. If Japanese subjects commit a crime involving Joseon people at the ports designated in Joseon, they shall all be tried and judged by Japanese officials. If Joseon people commit a crime involving Japanese, they shall all be investigated and handled by Joseon officials. Each shall judge according to the laws of its own country, without any shielding or favouritism, striving to make fairness and equity plain.

paragraphs.orig: 第十一款　兩國既經通好，須另設立通商章程，以便兩國商民；且並現下議立各條款中，更應補添細目，以便遵照條件。自今不出六個月，兩國另派委員，會朝鮮國京城或江華府商議定立。
paragraphs.reading: 제십일관 양국기경통호, 수령설립통상장정, 이편양국상민; 차병현하의립각조관중, 경응보첨세목, 이편준조조건. 자금불출육개월, 양국령파위원, 회조선국경성혹강화부상의정립.
paragraphs.en: Article 11. Now that the two countries have established friendly relations, a separate trade regulation must be established for the convenience of the merchants of both countries; and in addition, details must be added to supplement the articles now agreed, so that the provisions can be followed. Within six months from now, the two countries shall each send commissioners to meet at the Joseon capital or at Ganghwa Prefecture to deliberate and establish them.

paragraphs.orig: 第十二款　右十一款議定條約，以此日為兩國信守遵行之始，兩國政府不得復變革之，永遠信遵，以敦和好矣。為此，作約書二本，兩國委任大臣各鈐印，互相交付，以昭憑信。
paragraphs.reading: 제십이관 우십일관의정조약, 이차일위양국신수준행지시, 양국정부부득복변혁지, 영원신준, 이돈화호의. 위차, 작약서이본, 양국위임대신각검인, 호상교부, 이소빙신.
paragraphs.en: Article 12. The eleven articles above having been agreed as a treaty, this day shall be the beginning of the two countries' faithful observance; the two governments shall not alter it again, but shall faithfully follow it forever, so as to strengthen amity. To this end two copies of the treaty are made; the ministers commissioned by the two countries have each affixed their seals and exchanged them, as proof of good faith.
